Summoner's Rift: The Map Explained

Lanes, river, jungle, towers and epic monsters: a tour of the map and what every part of it is for.

The big picture

Summoner's Rift is a square map. The blue side team starts in the bottom-left corner and the red side team starts in the top-right. Three lanes connect the two bases: top runs along the left and top edges, mid goes straight through the center, and bot runs along the bottom and right edges.

A river cuts diagonally across the map from top-left to bottom-right, splitting it into two halves. Each team's half of the jungle is on its own side of the river.

Towers, inhibitors and the Nexus

Each lane has three towers per team: the outer, inner and inhibitor tower. Behind the inhibitor tower is the inhibitor itself. Two more towers guard the Nexus.

  • Towers shoot enemy minions and champions in range. They hit champions very hard early in the game.
  • Outer, inner and inhibitor towers each have 5 plates: pieces of armor that give gold when you break them. Plates stay on all game.
  • The first tower destroyed in the game gives +300 bonus gold, shared with nearby allies.
  • Destroying an inhibitor makes your team spawn super minions in that lane, which are very strong. Inhibitors grow back after a few minutes.
Pro tipA tower ignores you as long as there are minions to hit and you don't attack enemy champions. As soon as you hit an enemy champion under their tower, the tower targets you.

The jungle

The jungle is the maze of paths between the lanes. It holds jungle camps: neutral monsters that give gold and XP. The most important are the two buff camps:

  • Blue Sentinel (blue buff): gives ability haste and mana regeneration.
  • Red Brambleback (red buff): your attacks burn and slow enemies, plus health regeneration.

Other camps are Gromp, Murk Wolves, Raptors and Krugs. Camps first appear at 0:55 (Gromp and Krugs at 1:07). The Rift Scuttler, a crab in the river, appears at 2:55. The jungler is the one who farms these camps. See Jungle.

Epic monsters

The river has two big pits with powerful monsters that help the whole team:

MonsterWhereWhenWhat it gives
DragonsBottom pitFrom 5:00, then 5:00 after each killA permanent team buff. 4 dragons give a Dragon Soul.
Void GrubsTop pit8:00 (gone at 14:45)Extra damage against towers.
Rift HeraldTop pit15:00 (gone at 19:45)A summonable Herald that charges a tower for huge damage.
Baron NashorTop pit20:00A strong buff that powers up your minions.
Elder DragonBottom pitAfter a team gets Dragon SoulLets you execute low-health enemies.

Learn how to fight over these in Objectives: Dragons, Grubs, Herald and Baron. You can track their timers with our objective timer tool.

Fog of war and brushes

You can only see the parts of the map near your team's champions, minions, towers and wards. Everything else is covered by the fog of war: enemies there are invisible to you.

The tall grass patches are called brushes (or bushes). A champion inside a brush is hidden from enemies outside it, unless they have a ward there. Brushes are perfect for ambushes, and dangerous to walk into blindly.

Common mistakeWalking into a dark brush or jungle path alone with no vision. If you can't see it, assume an enemy might be there, especially when several enemies are missing from the map.

Faelights and other map features

Faelights are glowing spots in the jungle and river. If you place a ward on one, the ward gets extra sight range and briefly reveals more of the area around it. There are 8 at the start of the game, and 4 more appear when the map changes element after the second dragon.

After the second dragon, the whole map takes on that dragon's element (for example, Ocean or Infernal), which changes some terrain and plants. Read more about vision in Vision Basics: Wards and the Minimap.

Key takeaways

  • Three lanes (top, mid, bot), a river, and a jungle on each side.
  • Each lane has outer, inner and inhibitor towers; plates on them give gold all game.
  • Dragons are in the bottom pit; Grubs, Herald and Baron are in the top pit.
  • The fog of war hides enemies you can't see; brushes hide champions inside them.
  • Warding a Faelight gives that ward extra vision.
